title: ACT ON THE STAFF OF NATIONAL INTELLIGENCE SERVICE KOREA
full_text:
CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1 (Purpose) The purpose of this Act is to prescribe special cases concerning the State Public Officials Act with respect to the qualifications, appointment, education and training, service, remuneration, etc. of staff of the National Intelligence Service Korea, in light of the importance of their responsibilities and duties and the unique characteristics of their status and working conditions.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Nov. 22, 2011]

Article 2 (Classification of grades) (1) The staff of the National Intelligence Service (hereinafter referred to as "staff members") shall be classified into staff members in special service and in general service of Grades I through IX; provided, staff members in general service shall be deemed public officials in general service under Article 2 (2) 1 of the State Public Officials Act. <Amended on Jan. 7, 2014>
  (2) The classification of grades under paragraph (1) may not apply to staff members engaged in fields requiring specialized expertise and experience (hereinafter referred to as "professional official").
  (3) The name of each grade under paragraph (1) by type of duties, and the field of duties, treatment, etc. of professional officials under paragraph (2) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Nov. 22, 2011]

Article 3 (Staff members in fixed term positions) (1) The National Intelligence Service may appoint staff members in fixed term positions, if necessary, taking into account the details and specificity of its duties. <Amended on Jan. 7, 2014>
  (2) The staff members in fixed term positions shall be deemed public officials in fixed term positions under Article 26-5 (1) of the State Public Officials Act; provided, the requirements and procedures for appointment, maximum service age, and other necessary matters shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on Jan. 7, 2014>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Nov. 22, 2011]
  [Title Amended on Jan. 7, 2014]

Article 4 (Scope of application) (1) Except as otherwise provided in this Act, this Act shall not apply to the Director (hereinafter referred to as the "Director"), the Deputy Director, and the Executive Director of the National Intelligence Service, except for Chapter V.
  (2) Except as otherwise provided in this Act, this Act shall not apply to persons affiliated with institutions or organizations other than the National Intelligence Service, who are dispatched to work for it, except for Articles 13, 14, and 23, and Chapters V and IX.
  (3) Except as otherwise provided in this Act, this Act shall not apply to staff members in fixed term positions, except for Articles 8, 13, 14, 20, and 23 and Chapters V, VII, and IX. <Amended on Jan. 7, 2014>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Nov. 22, 2011]

Article 5 (Definitions) The terms used in this Act are defined as follows:
  1. The term "appointment" means new employment, promotion, salary grade elevation, reassignment, transfer, dispatch, voluntary demotion, leave of absence, suspension from office, demotion, reinstatement, dismissal, removal from office, and expulsion;
  2. The term "voluntary demotion" means an appointment to a lower grade within the same job series or to a lower grade in a different job series because there is no lower grade in the current job series;
  3. The term "reassignment" means an appointment in a different job series;
  4. The term "transfer" means a change of assigned position within the same grade;
  5. The term "reinstatement" means the restoration of a staff member who was on leave of absence or suspended from office, or unable to perform his or her duties due to demotion;
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Nov. 22, 2011]

CHAPTER II APPOINTMENT AND EXAMINATION

Article 6 (Appointment principles) (1) The appointment of a staff member shall be based on academic background, qualifications, experience, and age, and shall be determined through examinations, work records, and other evidence of competence.
  (2) The detailed scope, methods, procedures, etc. of appointment under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Nov. 22, 2011]

Article 7 (Appointing authority) (1) The President shall appoint staff members and professional officials of Grade V or higher upon the recommendation of the Director; provided, the President shall delegate the authority to appoint them to the Director, except for the following appointment authorities:
  1. Transfer, leave of absence, suspension from office, and reinstatement of Grade I staff members;
  2. New employment, promotion, voluntary demotion, demotion, dismissal, removal from office, and expulsion of staff members of Grades I through III.
  (2) Staff members of Grade VI or lower shall be appointed by the Director. <Amended on Jan. 7, 2014>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Nov. 22, 2011]

Article 8 (Qualifications for appointment and grounds for disqualification) (1) Staff members shall be appointed from among persons of sound mind and body and of good conduct.
  (2) Any of the following persons may not be appointed as a staff member: <Amended on Jan. 7, 2014; Jul. 20, 2021>
  1. A person who does not have the nationality of the Republic of Korea;
  2. A person who holds both the nationality of the Republic of Korea and that of a foreign country;
  3. A person under adult guardianship;
  4. A person who was declared bankrupt and has not yet been reinstated;
  5. A person sentenced to suspension of qualification or heavier punishment;
  6. A person who is under suspension of the sentence of imprisonment without labor or heavier punishment as declared by a court;
  7. A person dismissed due to disciplinary action.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Nov. 22, 2011]

Article 8-2 (Background investigation) (1) The Director shall conduct a background investigation of persons subject to appointment to verify matters related to Article 8 (1) and to assess their patriotism, sincerity, reliability, security, etc.
  (2) The detailed scope, methods, procedures, etc. of background investigations under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Nov. 22, 2011]

Article 9 (New employment) Staff members shall be newly employed through an open competitive examination for employment; provided, persons with special knowledge, experience, skills, or research records related to their duties may be recruited through a career-based competitive recruitment examination, etc. <Amended on Jan. 7, 2014>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Nov. 22, 2011]

Article 10 (Promotion) (1) The promotion of staff members shall be made based on work performance records, career evaluations, and verification of other abilities from among staff members of the immediate lower grade; provided, if Grade VI staff members are promoted to Grade V, they may also undergo a promotion examination, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on Jan. 7, 2014>
  (2) The minimum years of service required for promotion by grade and other matters necessary for promotion shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on Jan. 7, 2014>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Nov. 22, 2011]

Article 11 (Appointment examinations) The Director shall administer and manage appointment examinations of staff members.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Nov. 22, 2011]

CHAPTER III REMUNERATION

Article 12 (Remuneration) Remuneration for staff members shall be as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Nov. 22, 2011]

Article 13 (Compensation) Retired staff members who have sustained injuries in the course of arresting spies or performing national security duties equivalent thereto, their families and the bereaved family members of those who have died (including death resulting from injuries), as prescribed by Presidential Decree, shall be eligible for compensation under the Act on the Honorable Treatment of and Support for Persons of Distinguished Service to the State or the Act on Support for Persons Eligible for Veterans' Compensation. <Amended on Sep. 15, 2011>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Nov. 22, 2011]

CHAPTER IV EDUCATION

Article 14 (Education and training) (1) The Director shall provide education and training for staff members to enhance the efficiency of their duties.
  (2) The Director may entrust educational or research institutes at home and abroad with the education and training of staff members, if deemed necessary.
  (3) The results of education and training shall be reflected in personnel management.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Nov. 22, 2011]

CHAPTER V SERVICE

Article 15 (Oath) Before taking office, every staff member shall take the following oath in presence of the Director: "As a public official performing national security affairs, I swear to serve the State with unwavering patriotism and a strong sense of duty, and solemnly swear to abide by and obey all statutes or regulations as well as official orders, and to fulfill duties entrusted to me with creativity and sincerity."
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Nov. 22, 2011]

Article 16 (Prohibition of dereliction of duty) No staff member shall be derelict in the performance of his or her duties without permission from a superior or good cause.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Nov. 22, 2011]

Article 17 (Confidentiality) (1) No staff member shall disclose any confidential information acquired in the course of his or her duties, both during his or her tenure and after retirement.
  (2) If a staff member (including a retired person; hereafter in this Article the same shall apply) intends to testify or make a statement as a witness, expert witness, appraiser, or a party to a case regarding matters relating to confidential information gained in the course of his or her duties, he or she shall obtain prior permission from the Director.
  (3) A person with a legal interest in a case where he or she sought a staff member as a witness, expert witness, or appraiser, may apply for permission for testimony or statement by the staff member to the Director with the court’s approval, if he or she may face disadvantages if the staff member fails to apply for permission under paragraph (2).
  (4) In determining whether to grant permission pursuant to paragraph (2) or (3), the Director shall not refuse to grant permission, unless a disclosure would undermine vital national interests or seriously affect national security, such as military or diplomatic relations and inter-Korean relations.
  (5) A staff member shall obtain prior permission from the Director before publishing or publicly disclosing matters related to the National Intelligence Service’ duties through other means. In such cases, paragraph (4) shall apply mutatis mutandis.
  (6) If the Director grants permission for testimony or statement under paragraph (2) or (3), the court may take appropriate measures, such as restricting public disclosure of testimony to safeguard official secrets and other relevant interests.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Nov. 22, 2011]

Article 18 (Prohibition of for-profit business and concurrent officeholding) (1) A staff member may not engage in any for-profit business activity, other than the performance of his or her duties, or concurrently hold another office without permission from the Director.
  (2) The Director shall determine what constitutes for-profit business activities under paragraph (1).
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Nov. 22, 2011]

CHAPTER VI STATUS GUARANTEE

Article 19 (Involuntary status measures) No staff member shall be involuntarily demoted, placed on leave of absence or dismissed, except in cases where a sentence is imposed, a disciplinary action is taken, or other grounds prescribed in statutes apply; provided, this shall not apply to Grade I staff members.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Nov. 22, 2011]

Article 20 (Ipso facto retirement) If a staff member falls under any subparagraph of Article 8 (2) (excluding subparagraph 6), he or she shall retire ipso facto.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Nov. 22, 2011]

Article 21 (Ex officio dismissal) (1) When a staff member falls under any of the following subparagraphs, the appointing authority may dismiss him or her ex officio:
  1. Where he or she is unable to perform his or her duties due to a physical or mental disability;
  2. Where he or she is deemed unfit to be a staff member due to a significant lack of ability to perform his or her duties or an extremely poor work attitude;
  3. Where the position is eliminated or the quota is exceeded due to the revision or abolition of the organization or quotas, the reduction of budget, etc.;
  4. Where he or she fails to return to his or her duties or is unable to perform his or her duties without good cause after the period of leave of absence expires or after the grounds for leave of absence cease to exist;
  5. When he or she is disqualified as a result of the qualification examination under Article 21-2.
  (2) The consent of the Disciplinary Committee shall be obtained to dismiss a staff member under paragraph (1) 2.
  (3) When dismissing a staff member pursuant to paragraph (1) 3, the standards for dismissal shall be determined in consideration of the type of appointment, performance of duties, ability to perform duties, history of disciplinary actions, etc.
  (4) A Review Committee shall be established to determine standards for dismissal under paragraph (3) or to select persons subject to dismissal pursuant to paragraph (1) 3, with decisions made following deliberation and resolution by the committee.
  (5) The chairperson of the Review Committee under paragraph (4) shall be appointed by the Director from either the Deputy Director or the Executive Director, and the committee shall be comprised of not less than 5 but not more than 7 members designated by the Director from among the higher-ranking persons than those subject to dismissal, but if there are insufficient higher-ranking persons, the committee may consist of not more than 4 persons.
  (6) A staff member who has been dismissed pursuant to paragraph (1) 3 may be reappointed with preference if any vacancy occurs.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Nov. 22, 2011]

Article 21-2 (Qualification examination) (1) If a staff member has received the lowest grade in work performance ratings 2 consecutive times or at least 3 times within 10 years, he or she shall undergo a qualification examination.
  (2) A Qualification Examination Committee shall be established in the National Intelligence Service to conduct qualification examinations.
  (3) The Qualification Examination Committee shall consist of not less than 5 and not more than 7 members appointed by the Director from among the staff members of Grade II or higher at the National Intelligence Service, and the chairperson shall be appointed by the Director from either the Deputy Director or the Executive Director of the National Intelligence Service.
  (4) Qualification examinations shall be based on work performance ratings, and a person deemed unable to continue performing his or her duties shall be disqualified.
  (5) Matters necessary for the composition and operation of the Qualification Examination Committee and the standards for examination and processing thereof shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Nov. 22, 2011]

Article 22 (Retirement age) (1) Staff members’ retirement age shall be as follows: <Amended on Jan. 7, 2014>
  1. Retirement age: 60 years old;
  2. High year of tenure for staff members in special service:
    (a) Grade II staff members: 5 years;
    (b) Grade III staff members: 7 years;
    (c) Grade IV staff members: 12 years;
    (d) Grade V staff members: 18 years.
  (2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1) 2, the following subparagraphs shall apply to the high year of tenure of a staff member who has been demoted due to a disciplinary action (including demotion to Grade VI): <Amended on Jan. 7, 2014>
  1. The high year of tenure in a grade to which he or she is demoted shall be the same as the high year of tenure in the highest grade held before the demotion; provided, if a Grade I staff member is demoted, he or she may be dismissed;
  2. In calculating the high year of tenure, the years of service in the grade before and after demotion shall be aggregated.
  (3) If a staff member’s retirement date falls between January and June, he or she shall retire ipso facto on June 30, and if the date of his or her retirement falls between July and December, he or she shall retire ipso facto on December 31. <Amended on Jan. 7, 2014>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Nov. 22, 2011]

Article 22-2 (Support for employment of retired staff members) (1) In order to utilize the expertise of retired staff members (including prospective retirees) and to facilitate their smooth transition into society, the Director may provide employment support, such as career counseling, vocational guidance, and job placement services; start-up assistance such as start-up counseling or education; and career development support, etc. within the budget.
  (2) Matters necessary for support under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  [This Article Added on Oct. 19, 2021]

Article 23 (Investigation of staff members) (1) If an investigative agency intends to detain a staff member, it shall notify the Director in advance; provided, this shall not apply to flagrant offenders.
  (2) When an investigative agency detains a staff member who is a flagrant offender, it shall, without delay, notify the Director of such fact.
  (3) Upon commencing or completing an investigation of a staff member, an investigative agency shall, without delay, notify the Director of the investigation and the results of the investigation.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Nov. 22, 2011]

CHAPTER VII DISCIPLINARY ACTION

Article 24 (Grounds for disciplinary action) If a staff member falls under any of the following subparagraphs, a disciplinary action may be taken following a resolution on disciplinary action: <Amended on Jun. 9, 2020>
  1. Where he or she violates this Act or the State Public Officials Act and any order issued thereunder;
  2. Where he or she violates his or her official duties or neglects to perform his or her duties;
  3. Where he or she commits an act that undermines his or her dignity or reputation expected of any staff member, regardless of whether he or she is related to his or her duties.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Nov. 22, 2011]

Article 25 (Establishment of the Disciplinary Committee) (1) A Disciplinary Committee shall be established in the National Intelligence Service to examine and resolve on disciplinary cases involving staff members.
  (2) The composition, types, authority, examination procedures, and other necessary matters relating to the Disciplinary Committee shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Nov. 22, 2011]

Article 26 (Disciplinary procedures) Disciplinary action against staff members shall be imposed by the Director following a resolution by the Disciplinary Committee; provided, the President shall impose demotion, removal from office, or expulsion of staff members of Grade III or higher upon the recommendation of the Director following a resolution by the Disciplinary Committee.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Nov. 22, 2011]

Article 27 (Right of persons subject to disciplinary action to make statements) (1) A staff member subject to disciplinary action pending in the Disciplinary Committee may request an oral review to make an oral argument.
  (2) In cases falling under paragraph (1), the relevant staff member may appoint an assistant from among other staff members to make an argument.
  (3) A resolution on disciplinary action without granting the person subject to such action an opportunity to make a statement under paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be null and void, except when the person is in a foreign country.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Nov. 22, 2011]

Article 28 (Suspension of disciplinary procedures) If a case to be referred to disciplinary action is under criminal investigation, a request for a resolution on disciplinary action or other disciplinary procedures may not proceed from the date he or she is notified of the commencement of the investigation under Article 23 (3).
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Nov. 22, 2011]

Article 29 (Statue of limitation on grounds for disciplinary action) (1) No request for a resolution on disciplinary action shall be filed after the following periods have elapsed from the date the grounds for disciplinary action occurred: <Amended on Jan. 7, 2014; Oct. 19, 2021>
  1. Where the grounds for disciplinary action, etc. fall under any of the following: 10 years:
    (a) Prohibited acts under Article 4 of the Act on the Punishment of Arrangement of Commercial Sex Acts;
    (b) Sexual crimes defined in Article 2 of the Act on Special Cases concerning the Punishment of Sexual Crimes;
    (c) Sex offenses against children or youth defined in subparagraph 2 of Article 2 of the Act on the Protection of Children and Youth against Sex Offenses;
    (d) Sexual harassment under subparagraph 2 of Article 3 of the Framework Act on Gender Equality;
  2. Where the grounds for disciplinary action, etc. fall under any of the following: 5 years:
    (a) Disclosure of confidential information, involvement in politics, or abuse of power;
    (b) In cases falling under any subparagraph of Article 78-2 (1) of the State Public Officials Act;
  3. In cases of acts that constitute other grounds for disciplinary action, etc.: 3 years.
  (2) If the period referred to in paragraph (1) expires or has less than 1 month remaining due to failure to take disciplinary procedures pursuant to Article 28, the period referred to in paragraph (1) shall be deemed to expire on the day 1 month after the date of receipt of notice of the termination of an investigation under Article 23 (3).
  (3) If the Appeals Review Committee or a court decides to invalidate or revoke a disciplinary action on the grounds of defects in the composition of the Disciplinary Committee, flaws in resolution on disciplinary action or other procedures, or excessive severity of disciplinary action, a request for disciplinary action may be filed again, within 3 months from the date such decision becomes final and conclusive, notwithstanding paragraph (1).
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Nov. 22, 2011]

CHAPTER VIII SUPPLEMENTARY PROVISIONS

Article 30 (Application mutatis mutandis of the State Public Officials Act) Except as otherwise provided in this Act, the provisions governing public officials in general service under the State Public Officials Act shall apply mutatis mutandis to staff members; provided, this shall not apply to Articles 17, 18, and 73-3 of the State Public Officials Act.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Nov. 22, 2011]

Article 31 Deleted. <May 26, 2005>

CHAPTER IX PENALTY PROVISIONS

Article 32 (Penalty provisions) A person who violates Article 17 shall be punished by imprisonment with labor for not more than 10 years or by a fine not exceeding 10 million won.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Nov. 22, 2011]

Article 1 (Enforcement date)
This Act shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation.
Article 2 (Transitional measures concerning change of staff members in technical service or in contractual service into those in general service)
(1) Among staff members in technical service who are in service as at the time this Act enters into force, staff members in technical service of Grades III, IV, V, and VI shall be deemed appointed as Grade VI staff members in general service; Grade VII staff members in technical service as Grade VII staff members in general service; Grade VIII staff members in technical service as Grade VIII staff members in general service; and Grade IX staff members in technical service as Grade IX staff members in general service, respectively. In such cases, matters relating to job families, job series, classes shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(2) A staff member in contractual service who is in service as at the time this Act enters into force shall be deemed appointed as a staff member in a fixed term position on the enforcement date of this Act. In such cases, the period of service as a staff member in a fixed term position shall be the remainder of the contract period as at the time of his or her employment as a staff member in contractual service, and the remuneration during such period shall be governed by the contract in effect at the time of his or her employment.
Article 3 (Transitional measures concerning incompetent persons)
Persons under adult guardianship and persons under limited guardianship under the amended provisions of Article 8 (2) 3 shall be deemed to include persons for whom the declaration of incompetency or quasi-incompetency remains effective under Article 2 of the Addenda to the Civil Act (Act No. 10429).
Article 4 (Transitional measures concerning examinations underway)
(1) The examination for the appointment of staff members in technical service, and the examination for the employment of staff members in contractual service, both of which are underway as at the time this Act enters into force, shall be deemed the examination for the appointment of staff members in general service and the examination for the appointment of staff members in fixed term positions, respectively.
(2) A person who passed an examination prescribed in Article 4 (1) of the Addenda before this Act enters into force, but has not yet been appointed as at the time this Act enters into force, shall be deemed to have passed each of the examinations. In such cases, with respect to matters regarding appointment, the latter part of Article 2 (1) of the Addenda shall apply mutatis mutandis to staff members in general service, and the latter part of Article 2 (2) of the Addenda shall apply mutatis mutandis to staff members in fixed term positions.
Article 5 (Transitional measures concerning retirement age of staff members in technical service appointed to general service position)
(1) Notwithstanding the amended provisions of Article 22 (1) 1 of the Act, if staff members in technical service whose retirement age prescribed in the Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Staff of the National Intelligence Service Korea is 57 years old, are appointed to a general service position, the retirement age for those who reach the retirement age between 2014 and 2015, shall be 58 years old; for those who reach the retirement age between 2016 and 2018, shall be 59 years old; and for those who reach the retirement age from 2019 onward, shall be 60 years old.
(2) Notwithstanding the amended provisions of Article 22 (1) 1 of the Act, if staff members in technical service whose retirement age prescribed in the Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Staff of the National Intelligence Service is 55 years old, are appointed to a general service position, the retirement age for those who reach the retirement age in 2014, shall be 56 years old; the retirement age for those who reach the retirement age between 2015 and 2016, shall be 57 years old; the retirement age for those who reach the retirement age between 2017 and 2018, shall be 58 years old; the retirement age for those who reach the retirement age between 2019 and 2020, shall be 59 years old; and the retirement age for those who reach the retirement age in 2021 onward, shall be 60 years old, pursuant to the previous provisions.
